chunks: Abu Dawud from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Fadalah ibn Ayoub from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one with sexual impurity and the menstruating woman taking the chattel from the Masjid which happens to be in it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, but they should not place anything in the Masjid'.

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: The person in a state of major ritual impurity (Junub) who has not yet performed Ghusl.
key_terms.الْحَائِضِ: The menstruating woman, who is in a state of ritual impurity due to menses.
key_terms.الْمَتَاعَ: Chattel, goods, or items placed for use or storage.

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman or a Junubi person enter the mosque and handle items inside it?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between mere entry and the act of depositing belongings, affirming that major impurity (Junub) and menstruation (Haidh) do not invalidate the sanctity of the Masjid for them to handle items. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the prohibition on placing objects is specific to avoiding physical defilement of the space, rather than a general exclusion from the premises.
